meta.title: Cluster Policies: Five Fields That Can't Be Copied Verbatim

views.label: Five fields, five reasons
views.note: Node types, cloud attribute blocks, identity references, tags, and spark_conf all break in different ways across clouds.

views.label: As code, not console clicks
views.note: Terraform makes the target-cloud values explicit and reviewable instead of hidden in a UI form.

views.label: Tiers, not one policy per team
views.note: Teams map to workload tiers, tiers map to policies — not the other way around.

cards.title: Five fields, five different breaks
items: node_type_id names differ entirely across clouds, not just in value
aws_attributes / azure_attributes / gcp_attributes blocks don't transfer between clouds at all
custom_tags often encode the source cloud's account, subscription, or project ID

cards.title: Fixed fields, not conventions
items: No-public-IP, mandatory tags, and instance-profile restrictions belong in type: "fixed" fields
A convention can be silently overridden by an individual cluster config; a fixed policy field can't
Terraform makes every target-cloud value explicit and reviewable, not hidden in a console form

cards.title: Tiers, and re-tuned cost guardrails
items: One policy family per workload tier — etl-standard, ml-gpu, ad-hoc-notebook — not one per team
Max workers and auto-termination need re-review against target-cloud pricing, not a copied source limit
A policy tuned for source-cloud spot pricing may be wrong on the target by a wide margin
